summary.text: A 61-year-old man was examined by a local physician for constipation with abdominal pain. CT showed a thickened rectosigmoid colon wall, swollen regional lymph nodes and an obscure space-occupying lesion at S8 localized into the portal vein. After admission, colonography revealed a type 3 rectosigmoid tumor and CEA and CA19-9 were elevated. Emergency colonostomy was performed for obstructive colitis.

With suspicion of portal vein tumor thrombosis, he received 6 courses of mFOLFOX6 + panitumumab and, six months after admission, laparoscopic anterior resection. Pathology showed a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with final pathological stage IIIb. Six courses of adjuvant mFOLFOX6 followed, during which tumor marker levels were elevated.

PET after six courses of adjuvant chemotherapy showed abnormal accumulation with SUVmax 5.8 at P8. CT and MRI showed a portal vein lesion extending from S8 or P8 to S5 or P5. Right hemihepatectomy was performed; pathology showed the tumor thrombosis without hepatic parenchymal invasion and with a tumor-free cut surface. There were no specific postoperative complications, and he was discharged 13 days after the operation.

Paraaortic lymph node recurrence followed the hepatectomy; the abstract and the main text give different intervals. He is currently undergoing systemic chemotherapy, described in the discussion as second-line treatment, and the discussion reports survival of 15 months following the first surgery.
